text.p: Following are some of the
main stories in the Dutch newspapers this morning. Reuters has
not verified these stories and does not vouch for their
accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- The Netherlands Securities Board (STE) to probe into
possible insider trading in Toolex Alpha shares. (p1)
- Temp agency Unique aims for a bourse launch to finance its
international expansion plans. (p1)
- Number of unemployed stops falling after 30 months. (p1)
- Trading and installation group Internatio-Mueller takes
over all remaining shares of automation firm Turnkiek Holding.
- Fokker Space unit Fokker Control Systems gets Dfl 8 mln
order for testing equipment for Indonesia's aircraft maker IPTN.
- US publisher Mc Graw-Hill to compete with Dutch publishers
Reed Elsevier and Wolters-Kluwer with scientific publications on
the Internet. (p3)
- Retailer Ahold starts 50-50 joint venture with China
Venturetech Investment Corp to develop and operate supermarkets
in Shanghai. (p5)
- Royal Dutch/Shell to double its investments in Poland to $
60 mln next year. (p5)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Parliamentary motion by Liberals against tobacco excise
hike might find support. (p1)
- Bank insurer Fortis, who are to take over MeesPierson from
ABN Amro bank, finds skeleton in the merchant bank's cupboard.
- Traffic minister orders Dutch PTT (KPN) to cut ties with
cable operator Casema. (p2)
- Public prosecutor calls in an outsider to help with probe
into BolsWessanen insider trading case. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch counter intelligence says it has signs that
activists protesting expansion of Schiphol Airport may turn to
violent actions. (p1)
- Labour Party wants to pressure businesses to invest in the
environment. (p7)
- Philips Electronics to build telecom plant in Indonesia.
- KLM partner Northwest Airlines' profit growth continues.
TROUW
- Former Fokker chief Ben van Schaik does not believe a
restart is possible for the bankrupt aircraft maker. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Temp agency Randstad investigates possibility of mobile
medical teams that can perform operations on demand. (p1)
- KLM to increase productivity through fleet expansion and
more efficient use of existing planes. (p15)
